name: Target source (sub-facet root)
characteristic: who or what produced the quantity the procedure is driven toward
positive_test: the procedure is fitted to something; name what supplies it
negative_test: the procedure fits nothing
examples: all values below
notes: multi-valued

name: External annotation
characteristic: what kind of agent produced the annotation
positive_test: the target was produced by an agent outside the run's own model and environment
negative_test: the target is computed from the input itself
examples: labels, preferences, demonstrations

name: Human-produced labels
positive_test: a person assigned the target value to the example
negative_test: a model or a rule assigned it
examples: ImageNet labels, annotated spans, human ratings

name: Model-produced targets
positive_test: another trained model produced the target the learner is fitted to
negative_test: the learner produced its own target
examples: knowledge distillation teacher logits, synthetic instruction data, RLAIF labels, pseudo-labels from a different model
notes: distinct from self-labelling, which is S.src.self.own

name: Programmatic and weak labels
positive_test: a rule, heuristic, lexicon or metadata field supplied the target
negative_test: a human adjudicated each example
examples: Snorkel labelling functions, distant supervision, regex labels, metadata-derived labels

name: Comparisons and rankings
positive_test: the target is a relative judgement between two or more candidates, not an absolute value
negative_test: the target is an absolute score or class
examples: RLHF comparison pairs, learning-to-rank relevance judgements, KTO thumbs

name: Expert demonstrations
positive_test: the target is an action sequence produced by an expert acting in the task
negative_test: the target is a scalar score of the agent's own behaviour
examples: behaviour-cloning trajectories, DAgger corrections, teleoperated robot data

name: Naturally co-occurring pairs
positive_test: supervision comes from items that were observed together in the world, not annotated
negative_test: an annotator created the association
examples: image-alt-text pairs for CLIP, audio-video sync, translation bitext, click logs
notes: boundary between supervised and self-supervised

name: Measured outcome variable
positive_test: the target is a quantity recorded as an attribute of the unit -- an outcome, a response, a measurement -- including a categorical response, with no annotator deciding it for the purpose of supervision
negative_test: a value an annotator assigned to an example in order to supervise a model (S.src.ext.human); a value a rule computed (S.src.ext.prog)
examples: the response in a regression, the outcome in a trial, a survival time, a measured covariate
notes: added after pinning: 169 nodes across the classical branch were parked on the interior node S.src.ext for want of this, so every S.src.ext.* roll-up read `unknown annotation type` when the truth is `no annotator exists`. Tests sharpened during the migration: the first wording did not separate a respondent from an annotator, and ~40 tree/ensemble/GLM nodes turn entirely on that -- a diagnosis or a survey answer is person-assigned but is not an annotation

name: Environment feedback
positive_test: the target is feedback returned after the system acted
negative_test: the target exists before the system acts
examples: game score, verifier pass/fail, curiosity bonus

name: Task reward from the environment
positive_test: an external environment or simulator emits the scalar being maximised
negative_test: the scalar is computed by a model the run also trained
examples: Atari score, MuJoCo reward, game win/loss

name: Programmatic verifier reward
positive_test: a deterministic checker decides correctness of the produced output
negative_test: a learned model judges the output
examples: unit-test pass, exact-match answer check, compiler success, formal proof check
notes: the RLVR branch

name: Learned reward model
positive_test: the reward is emitted by a model fitted on external judgements
negative_test: the reward comes from the environment directly
examples: RLHF reward models, process reward models, LLM-as-judge reward
notes: derived from preferences, hence multi-parent

name: Intrinsic reward
positive_test: the reward is computed from the agent's own prediction error, novelty or counts
negative_test: the reward is supplied from outside the agent
examples: RND bonus, ICM error, pseudo-counts, empowerment, DIAYN diversity reward

name: The input itself
characteristic: which part of the input plays the role of target
positive_test: the target is a deterministic function of the unlabelled input
negative_test: a separate agent or environment supplied the target
examples: masked tokens, augmented views, noise added by the method

name: Hidden part of the input
positive_test: part of the input is removed and the procedure predicts exactly what was removed
negative_test: the input is perturbed but nothing is withheld for prediction
examples: BERT masked tokens, MAE masked patches, span corruption, inpainting

name: The next or future element
positive_test: the target is the continuation of an observed prefix, in time or sequence order
negative_test: the target is a hidden element of a bidirectional context
examples: next-token prediction, PixelCNN, future-frame prediction, CPC futures

name: A second view of the same instance
positive_test: two transformed copies of one instance are made and compared to each other
negative_test: one copy only, compared to a stored label
examples: SimCLR views, BYOL views, SwAV views, multi-crop

name: A deliberately corrupted copy
positive_test: noise of known magnitude is added and the procedure must undo or score it
negative_test: a transformation whose inverse is not the learning target
examples: DDPM noise, denoising autoencoder noise, score matching perturbation

name: The input itself, unmodified
positive_test: the target is the whole input, reproduced with no part hidden and no noise added
negative_test: part of the input is withheld or corrupted first
examples: autoencoder reconstruction, VAE reconstruction term, PCA reconstruction, self-reconstruction losses
notes: added after the VAE worked example found no fitting value

name: The model's own prior output
positive_test: the learner's own current, averaged or past prediction serves as the target
negative_test: another model produced the target
examples: pseudo-labelling, Mean Teacher EMA targets, self-training, self-consistency, bootstrapped values
notes: includes RL bootstrapping

name: Structure of the unlabelled data
positive_test: the objective is defined on the geometry or statistics of the whole dataset, not per example
negative_test: a per-example target
examples: k-means distortion, PCA variance, t-SNE neighbourhoods, topic-model likelihood
notes: the classical-unsupervised home

name: Identification by study design
characteristic: what feature of the design creates the counterfactual contrast
positive_test: the target is a contrast between conditions that a design argues is comparable
negative_test: the target is a predictive association with no comparability claim
examples: RCT arms, propensity-matched pairs, instrument, discontinuity

name: Randomised assignment
positive_test: treatment was assigned at random by the experimenter
negative_test: treatment was observed as it occurred
examples: A/B tests, randomised controlled trials, randomised encouragement

name: Conditional comparability
positive_test: comparability is claimed after conditioning on measured covariates
negative_test: comparability comes from an instrument, threshold or time structure
examples: propensity matching, IPW, AIPW, double ML, g-computation

name: Quasi-experimental structure
positive_test: comparability comes from an instrument, a threshold or a pre/post panel
negative_test: comparability comes from covariate adjustment alone
examples: 2SLS instruments, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, synthetic control

name: Conditional-independence signal
positive_test: the signal is the pattern of statistical (in)dependences used to orient edges
negative_test: the signal is an effect magnitude
examples: PC algorithm tests, FCI, GES score differences, LiNGAM non-Gaussianity

name: Known law or constraint
characteristic: what kind of prior knowledge is imposed
positive_test: the target is the residual of an equation or constraint assumed true a priori
negative_test: a target measured from data
examples: PDE residuals, conservation laws, logical constraints

name: Differential-equation residual
positive_test: the loss contains the residual of a differential equation evaluated at sampled points
negative_test: the equation is used only to generate training data
examples: PINN residual loss, Deep Ritz, Hamiltonian NN constraint

name: Symbolic or logical constraint
positive_test: the loss penalises violation of a declared logical or algebraic constraint
negative_test: the constraint is enforced by construction in the architecture
examples: semantic loss, constraint-satisfaction penalties, Lagrangian constraint terms
notes: speculative outside neuro-symbolic venues

name: A measured score from the run itself
positive_test: the target is a performance figure the procedure obtained by running or simulating a candidate -- a validation score, a held-out metric, a win rate, a fitness
negative_test: a reward emitted by an environment the agent acted in (S.src.env.reward); a target attached to an example (S.src.ext.*)
examples: AutoAugment's validation accuracy, NAS-RL's accuracy reward, Bayesian-optimisation observations, Hyperband budgets, MAP-Elites fitness
notes: added in D.1: four of six pinning regions proposed this gap independently under four different names (S.form.sel.metric, S.src.meas, S.src.env.metric, S.src.trial), which is the strongest convergence signal this process produced. It sits under S.src rather than S.src.ext because the quantity is produced by the run, not supplied to it

name: No training target
positive_test: the procedure has no quantity it is fitted to; it transforms or selects instead
negative_test: any fitted parameter, even a single calibration statistic
examples: beam search, top-p sampling, BPE merges (counting, not fitting), CutMix, gradient clipping, FSDP sharding
notes: essential: roughly a third of the dimension sits here

name: Comparison form (sub-facet root)
characteristic: how the gap between model output and target is turned into a number
positive_test: name the functional form of the training criterion
negative_test: the procedure has no criterion
examples: all values below
notes: multi-valued

name: Exact likelihood
positive_test: maximises a normalised log-probability the model can compute exactly
negative_test: maximises a bound or an unnormalised score
examples: cross-entropy, autoregressive LM loss, GLM likelihood, normalizing-flow likelihood, MLE

name: Variational bound
positive_test: maximises a tractable lower bound on an intractable log-likelihood
negative_test: maximises the exact likelihood
examples: ELBO, IWAE bound, variational EM, SVI, beta-VAE objective

name: Score and denoising criteria
positive_test: regresses the gradient of the log-density, or equivalently the added noise
negative_test: regresses the clean data point itself
examples: score matching, denoising score matching, DDPM epsilon-prediction, flow-matching velocity

name: Reconstruction error
positive_test: penalises a distance between a reconstruction and the original input
negative_test: penalises a distance between two different instances' representations
examples: autoencoder MSE, MAE pixel loss, PCA reconstruction, VQ codebook loss

name: Contrastive criteria
positive_test: the loss has explicit negatives whose similarity is pushed down
negative_test: the loss only pulls positives together
examples: InfoNCE, NT-Xent, triplet loss, BPR pairwise loss, noise-contrastive estimation

name: Agreement to a target network
positive_test: regresses one branch onto a target branch, with no negatives and a stop-gradient or EMA
negative_test: uses negatives, or a fixed external label
examples: BYOL, SimSiam, Mean Teacher consistency, SPR latent loss, data2vec
notes: collapse-avoidance is the signature

name: Decorrelation criteria
positive_test: drives an embedding cross-correlation or covariance matrix toward a target structure
negative_test: compares individual sample pairs
examples: Barlow Twins, VICReg, W-MSE, whitening losses

name: Margin criteria
positive_test: penalises violations of a required separation between scores
negative_test: penalises probability error
examples: hinge loss, SVM margin, triplet margin, large-margin softmax

name: Distortion and assignment criteria
positive_test: minimises total distance of points to assigned representatives or a layout
negative_test: minimises a probabilistic loss
examples: k-means distortion, MDS stress, t-SNE KL over neighbour distributions, OT cost

name: Adversarial equilibrium
positive_test: the criterion is a minimax between two optimisers with opposed objectives
negative_test: both terms are minimised by the same optimiser
examples: GAN objective, WGAN critic, DANN domain adversary, adversarial training inner max, GAIL

name: Expected-return maximisation
positive_test: maximises a discounted sum of future scalars, with credit assigned across time
negative_test: maximises a per-example score with no temporal credit
examples: policy gradient surrogates, Bellman TD error, PPO clipped surrogate, Q-learning loss

name: Distribution matching
positive_test: minimises an explicit divergence or moment discrepancy between two distributions
negative_test: minimises a per-example loss
examples: MMD, CORAL, KL to a teacher, Sinkhorn divergence, moment matching
notes: distillation's form when it is not plain cross-entropy

name: Estimating-equation solving
positive_test: chooses parameters by setting a sample moment or influence-function equation to zero
negative_test: minimising a loss by descent
examples: method of moments, GMM-IV, Z-estimation, TMLE targeting step, estimating equations in GEE
notes: added after the TMLE worked example found no fitting value

name: Ranking and preference criteria
positive_test: the loss depends only on the order of scores, not their absolute values
negative_test: the loss depends on absolute score values
examples: DPO loss, Bradley-Terry likelihood, LambdaRank, ListNet, pairwise ranking loss
notes: Bradley-Terry is also a likelihood; both values apply

name: Constraint residual
positive_test: penalises violation of an equation or constraint evaluated on sampled points
negative_test: penalises distance to observed data
examples: PINN PDE residual, Lagrangian penalty, semantic loss

name: Posterior targeting
positive_test: the procedure's criterion is correctness of a posterior, whether approached by sampling or obtained in closed form
negative_test: the criterion is a point estimate's loss
examples: MCMC detailed balance, SMC weighting, Bayes rule updates
notes: no gradient descent needed to satisfy it; test widened after pinning: it said `approached by sampling`, which excluded the closed-form posteriors of Gaussian processes, Kalman filters, Laplace approximation and expectation propagation -- about 25 of its own 53 pins contradicted it

name: Confidence and entropy criteria
positive_test: the criterion is a function of the model's own output confidence only
negative_test: the criterion involves any target outside the model's output
examples: entropy minimisation (TENT), confidence penalty, FixMatch thresholding, pseudo-label confidence gating

name: Sparsity and complexity criteria
positive_test: penalises the number or magnitude of active components, independent of fit
negative_test: penalises fit error
examples: L1 penalty, nuclear norm, MDL, AIC/BIC selection, sparse-autoencoder L1
notes: usually appears alongside a fit term

name: Invariance and robustness criteria
positive_test: penalises variation of the output under a declared nuisance transformation or environment
negative_test: penalises error on the observed distribution only
examples: IRM penalty, consistency regularisation, GroupDRO worst-group risk, VAT

name: Coverage criteria
positive_test: targets a stated frequency guarantee on a held-out distribution
negative_test: targets average accuracy
examples: conformal quantile calibration, conformal risk control, quantile pinball loss

name: Comparison of candidates by a measured score
positive_test: candidates are ranked or selected by a measured figure of merit, with no loss differentiated and no parameters updated by it
negative_test: a differentiable validation loss (that is an ordinary criterion); a reward maximised by a policy-gradient estimator (S.form.return)
examples: hyperparameter search, evolutionary and reinforcement-learning architecture search, population-based training, augmentation-policy search
notes: added in D.1 with S.src.meas. Every other S.form value is a criterion an optimiser minimises; selecting configurations by a held-out number is not, which is why all of L.hpo, L.nas and L.automl resolved to nothing

name: Assessment of an estimate
positive_test: compares replicate, permuted or held-out values of a statistic in order to quantify its error, coverage or significance, fitting no parameters in the process
negative_test: a criterion that parameters are fitted to; selecting among candidates by a measured score (S.form.metric)
examples: the bootstrap, jackknife, permutation tests, k-fold cross-validation as an error estimate, Neyman-Pearson tests, FDR control
notes: added 2026-10-07, closing the last non-data-dependent item on #96. The owner ruled assessment procedures in scope, which left L.boot and L.test (27 nodes) resolving to no signal: S.form.none is false for a bootstrap interval, because it genuinely does compare something. It is distinct from S.form.metric -- that one selects a candidate, this one quantifies an error

name: No criterion
positive_test: the procedure performs no comparison between an output and a target
negative_test: any fitted or calibrated quantity
examples: beam search, all-reduce, pipeline scheduling, magnitude pruning, BPE
